seasons.nouvel-an-hmong: Hmong New Year in Cacao (3–4 days)

climate.label: Long dry season
climate.note: The best time: September and October are the sunniest months.

climate.label: Short rainy season
climate.note: Sun and showers alternate, often late in the day.

climate.label: Little summer of March
climate.note: A 1 to 3 week lull, varying from year to year.

climate.label: Long rainy season
climate.note: May and June are the wettest. Superb forest, tracks sometimes difficult.

rules: Never go into the forest alone and always leave your route and return time with someone.
Stay on marked trails: you get lost very fast in the forest, even 50 m from a path.
Carry at least 1.5 L of water per person, a torch, a whistle, a charged phone and a power bank.
Mobile signal disappears away from the coast: download your guides before you go.
Swimming: the sea can be rough with currents. No river swimming without local advice.
Mosquitoes: repellent, long sleeves in the evening. Dengue is present in French Guiana.
Wildlife: don't touch frogs, snakes or caterpillars; shake out your shoes in the morning at a carbet.
Turtles: no white light or flash, never touch or block the animal.

cayenne-1j.title: Cayenne in a day
cayenne-1j.pitch: The old town, the market, culture, and sunset on the beach.
notes: Phở breakfast in the market hall.
Understand the peoples of French Guiana.
Sunset; turtles from April to August.

ile-nature.title: Cayenne island, forest side
ile-nature.pitch: Forest, Jesuit ruins and mangrove without leaving town.

kourou-salut.title: Kourou & Salvation Islands
kourou-salut.pitch: Space and the penal colony, two sides of Kourou.

cacao-kaw.title: Cacao & Kaw marsh
cacao-kaw.pitch: A Hmong Sunday, then a night in France's largest marsh.
notes: Botanical trail on the Kaw road.
Night caiman outing with a licensed guide.

ouest-3j.title: The West: penal colony, river and turtles
ouest-3j.pitch: The western road to the Maroni and the leatherback beach.

grand-sud.title: Deep South: Saül
grand-sud.pitch: Primary forest at the heart of the Amazonian Park, no roads.

palmistes.desc: Historic heart of Cayenne: a large square planted with royal palms, lined with Creole houses and government buildings.
tips: Ideal starting point for a walk around the old town.
Nicer late in the afternoon, when the heat drops.

ceperou.desc: Hill with the remains of the fort where Cayenne was founded. Views over the city, the estuary and the ocean.
tips: Short climb from Place Grenoble.
The best free view of Cayenne at sunset.

marche-cayenne.name: Cayenne Market
marche-cayenne.desc: Large covered market: fruit, spices, crafts and, under the hall, the famous morning Vietnamese soups (phở).
tips: Come in the morning: that's when it all happens.
Days and hours vary, check on site.

musee-cultures.desc: Collections on the peoples of French Guiana: Amerindian, Bushinengue, Creole, Hmong. The best introduction to the territory's diversity.
tips: Visit early in your stay to understand the rest.

montjoly.name: Montjoly Beach
montjoly.desc: Long sandy beach in Rémire-Montjoly. In season, a major nesting site for leatherback and olive ridley turtles, with guides from the Kwata association.
tips: At night: no white light, no flash, keep your distance.
Brown sea: that's normal, it's sediment from the Amazon.
montjoly.season: Sea turtle nesting: April → August; hatchlings until about October.

salines.name: Salines Trail
salines.desc: Walk through the wetlands behind Montjoly beach: mangrove, shorebirds, seaside atmosphere.
tips: Early morning for birds.
Mosquito repellent is a must.

rorota.name: Rorota Trail
rorota.desc: Forest hike on the Mahury hills around the Rorota lakes, with ocean views. Real forest 15 min from Cayenne.
tips: Start early, take 1.5 L of water.
Slippery after rain: wear shoes with grip.

bourda.desc: Forest hill trail with views over the coast. Popular with locals in the late afternoon.
tips: Busy in the evening: go in a group.

loyola.name: Loyola Plantation
loyola.desc: Ruins of a 17th–18th-century Jesuit plantation (sugar mill, chapel, pottery) in the woods, linked to the Mahury trail network.
tips: Combine it with Rorota in the same morning.

diamant.desc: 19th-century coastal battery at the mouth of the Mahury, at the end of the beach road.
tips: Lovely light in the late afternoon.

matoury.desc: Forest nature reserve on the edge of town: marked trails, rich biodiversity, a real forest feel.
tips: Stay on the marked trails.

cacao.name: Cacao, Hmong village
cacao.desc: Village founded by Hmong refugees from Laos in the late 1970s, about 1 h from Cayenne. Sunday market: fruit, vegetables, Hmong embroidery and Asian food under the halls.
tips: Sunday is the only market day: THE day to go.
Insect museum in the village.
Hmong New Year in December (3–4 days).

molokoi.name: Molokoï Trail
molokoi.desc: Long forest hike linking Cacao to the Kaw mountain, with bivouac shelters. Short out-and-back version from Cacao.
tips: Full version: fit adults, hammock and supplies.
Start: in Cacao, road on the left just after the market, then 600 m.
Tell someone your route (see Emergency).

roura.name: Roura village
roura.desc: Village on the Oyak river, gateway to the Kaw road and Cacao. Church, riverbanks, riverside atmosphere.
tips: A natural stop on the Kaw road.

tresor.name: Trésor Reserve
tresor.desc: Regional nature reserve on the road to the Kaw mountain: botanical trail in rainforest, accessible to all.
tips: A great first forest experience for families.

kaw.name: Kaw Marsh
kaw.desc: France's largest wetland (~94,700 ha), a nature reserve. Black caimans, scarlet ibis, herons, hoatzins. Explore by canoe, day or night.
tips: The night caiman outing is the highlight.
Easier access in the dry season.
Go with a licensed guide: you don't venture into the marsh alone.

csg.name: Guiana Space Centre & Space Museum
csg.desc: Europe's spaceport (Ariane 6, Vega-C). Guided tours of the site by booking, and the Space Museum.
tips: Book the tour in advance, ID required.
See the Events tab for upcoming launches.

kourou-plage.name: Kourou seafront
kourou-plage.desc: Beaches, Pointe des Roches and the Dreyfus tower. One of the public spots to watch a rocket lift off.
tips: On launch days, some areas of Kourou and the islands are closed.
Arrive early: launches draw crowds.

salut.name: Salvation Islands
salut.desc: Archipelago off Kourou (Île Royale, Saint-Joseph, Devil's Island): penal colony ruins, forest, clear water, free-roaming monkeys and agoutis.
tips: Shuttle or catamaran from Kourou: about €50 return (indicative, check).
Devil's Island can't be visited (landing forbidden).
Closed on some launch days: check Events.

zoo.name: Guiana Zoo
zoo.desc: Zoological park in Macouria, deep in the forest: about 450 animals, mostly Guianese wildlife (jaguar, tapir, harpy eagle…). Shaded walking circuit.
tips: The surest way to see large animals you almost never meet in the forest.

annamites.name: Annamite penal camp
annamites.desc: Ruins of a 1930s penal camp where Indochinese prisoners were held, swallowed by the forest.
tips: A place of memory: respect the ruins.

yiyi.name: Yiyi marshes
yiyi.desc: Marshes (pripris) near Sinnamary with trails and hides: waterbirds, spectacled caimans.
tips: Early morning or late afternoon.

iracoubo.name: Painted church of Iracoubo
iracoubo.desc: Church entirely hand-painted by a convict in the late 19th century. A surprising stop on the road west.
tips: The perfect break on the Cayenne → Saint-Laurent drive.

transportation.desc: Arrival camp for all convicts sent to French Guiana, now a historic monument. Guided tour of the cells (including the one attributed to Papillon) and interpretation centre.
tips: Take the guided tour: it gives the place its full meaning.
Saint-Laurent is also nice by bike.

relegation.desc: Former camp for 'relégués' (repeat offenders) at Saint-Jean-du-Maroni, a few kilometres from Saint-Laurent.
tips: Guided tours by appointment, only on some days: ask at the Saint-Laurent tourist office.

maroni.name: Maroni riverbanks
maroni.desc: The border river with Suriname, its canoes and constant comings and goings. Starting point for trips up the Maroni.
tips: Sunset over the river.
Crossings to Albina: ID needed, check the rules.

javouhey.name: Javouhey, Hmong market
javouhey.desc: French Guiana's second Hmong village (Mana), more traditional than Cacao. Sunday morning market: farm produce, embroidery, Hmong soup, sticky rice.
tips: Combine with Mana and Les Hattes on the same weekend.

mana.name: Mana village
mana.desc: Village founded in 1828 by Anne-Marie Javouhey on the Mana river: church, old houses, convent.
tips: On the way to Awala-Yalimapo.

hattes.name: Les Hattes Beach (Awala-Yalimapo)
hattes.desc: Historic leatherback nesting beach in the Amana Nature Reserve, on Kali'na land. Populations have dropped sharply: a hatchery now protects the nests.
tips: Follow reserve rules strictly: no light, no flash, keep your distance.
Kali'na Amerindian village: you are a guest, respect the place.
hattes.season: Leatherbacks: ~March → July; green turtles too. Season ends late August.

saint-georges.desc: Border town with Brazil (Oiapoque), linked by the Oyapock bridge. River, canoes, Franco-Brazilian atmosphere.
tips: Long highway (~190 km from Cayenne): leave with a full tank.
Crossing into Brazil: check documents and rules first.

saul.name: Saül, heart of the Amazonian Park
saul.desc: Village in the centre of French Guiana, reachable only by air, at the heart of the Amazonian Park. Network of marked trails in primary forest.
tips: No road: flights from Cayenne, limited seats.
Check with the Guiana Amazonian Park before you go.

maripasoula.name: Maripasoula & upper Maroni
maripasoula.desc: France's largest municipality, on the upper Maroni. Reached by plane or a long canoe trip upriver; gateway to the river villages.
tips: Some areas of the Amazonian Park require a permit.

franconie.desc: Departmental museum in a Creole house in central Cayenne, near Place des Palmistes: history of French Guiana, Amerindian, Bushinengue and Creole crafts, paintings by the convict Francis Lagrange.
tips: Limited hours that vary by day: check before you go.
Combine with Place des Palmistes, a short walk away.

montabo.name: Montabo coastal trail
montabo.desc: Easy, well-marked seaside walk north of Cayenne, ending on an often deserted beach. Another trail climbs Montabo hill.
tips: Best early morning or late afternoon.
Swimming: follow the signs at Montabo's lifeguarded beaches.

vidal.name: Vidal plantation trail
vidal.desc: Forest path of nearly 3 km to the ruins of the Vidal plantation, a former slave plantation. Protected Conservatoire du littoral site, managed by the Kwata association.
tips: Poorly signposted start, between the stadium and the Léon-Gontran-Damas high school.
Toucans and aracaris often seen early in the morning.

topu.name: Montagne Topu trail
topu.desc: 3.3 km marked loop on the Mahury heights, between the Rorota lakes and the Loyola trail. Panels on over 10,000 years of human presence in the area.
tips: Two starts: from the Rorota trail or from Loyola.
Viewpoint over the lakes, sometimes hidden by vegetation.

fourgassie.name: Fourgassié Falls
fourgassie.desc: Small waterfalls and clear pools in primary forest along the Fourgassié creek, on the Kaw road about 40 minutes from Cayenne.
tips: The rocks are very slippery: wear shoes with grip.
Avoid after heavy rain, the creek rises fast.

coq-de-roche.name: Cock-of-the-rock Trail
coq-de-roche.desc: Short trail (about 1.5 km out and back) in the Trésor/Kaw-Roura nature reserve, to a breeding area of the Guianan cock-of-the-rock, an iconic orange bird.
tips: Start on the Kaw road, after Camp Caïman, just before the sawmill.
Silence and binoculars: don't approach nesting sites.
The trail may close temporarily: check live conditions above.

roche-virginie.desc: Granite inselberg rising from the forest between Régina and Saint-Georges. Marked trail of about 6.5 km out and back through primary forest to a view over the canopy. Reserve managed by the ONF.
tips: Park on the RN2, a few kilometres after the Approuague bridge.
The rock is very slippery when wet.
Dry season (July to November) recommended.

maripa.desc: A series of rapids on the Oyapock, about twenty kilometres from Saint-Georges: shelter, forest botanical trail, swimming and rafting.
tips: About 19 km of track from the RN2: 4x4 almost essential.
Also reachable by canoe from Saint-Georges.
Take your rubbish back with you.

montagne-singes.name: Monkey Mountain
montagne-singes.desc: Forest trail on a 161 m hill south-west of Kourou. At the top, the shelter overlooks the canopy, the Space Centre, Kourou and its river. CNES land managed by the ONF.
tips: From the RN1, follow "Montagne des Singes / Dégrad Saramaka", parking after about 8 km.
Steep and slippery after rain.
Blue morphos common; monkeys rarer.

bois-diable.name: Bois Diable Lake
bois-diable.desc: Lake in town in Kourou, listed as a monitored bathing site: a freshwater alternative when the sea is rough.
tips: Check the water quality notice before swimming.

voltaire.name: Voltaire Falls
voltaire.desc: Falls of about 35 m on the Voltaire creek, a protected site south of Saint-Laurent. Reached via the Paul Isnard track (about 70 km), then on foot. Inn with hammocks at the end of the track.
tips: 4x4 recommended, the track deteriorates in the rainy season.
Plan the whole day, or a night there in a hammock.
No signal: leave your return time (Emergency).

marche-slm.name: Saint-Laurent Market
marche-slm.desc: The big market of western French Guiana, a few streets from the river: fruit, vegetables, spices and Maroni cooking.
tips: Come early, before the heat.
Bring cash.
marche-slm.when: Wednesday and Saturday mornings (to be confirmed)
